title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions
authors: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar, Krishan Saraswat
abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes by analyzing the spectral edges of the Double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. It successfully extends this methodology to supersymmetric $\mathcal{N}=1$ systems, demonstrating that these volumes arise naturally from the model's density of states in specific scaling limits. This provides a powerful, unified framework connecting random matrix theory, quantum gravity, and quantum field theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to determine $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson (WP) volumes, particularly extending the analysis to supersymmetric $\mathcal{N}=1$ extensions.
main_result: The authors show that $q$-deformed WP volumes can be derived from the spectral edges of the Double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model, providing a systematic way to construct these volumes in supersymmetric contexts.
method: The approach combines topological recursion, the ODE method, and analyzing scaling limits (e.g., $q 	o 1$) applied to the density of states derived from the DSSYK model.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model, which is used to generate spectral curves and density of states. The analysis extends this to $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric extensions.
key_observables: Weil-Petersson volumes ($V_{WP}$), $q$-deformed WP volumes ($V_{qWP}$), and the spectral density $ho_0(E)$.
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $q$, the scaling limit $q 	o 1$, and the boundary conditions (soft vs. hard edges).
main_assumptions: The results rely on identifying the top-degree parts of discrete volumes and assuming that the spectral edge analysis correctly captures the geometric invariants.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the connection between $q$-deformed volumes and the DSSYK spectral curve, then applying this framework to the soft and hard edges of the $N=1$ DSSYK model to derive candidate super WP volumes.
why_interesting: The connection between geometric invariants (WP volumes) and the spectral properties of complex quantum many-body models like SYK provides deep insights into the structure of quantum gravity and random matrix theory, which often informs condensed matter theories.
